notes_redacted: Path-traversal hardening for matchFileSnapshot is correct: resolves filePath against root (default process.cwd()) and rejects paths escaping root via startsWith(root+sep) with an explicit root-equality edge case. All fs operations now use the validated resolved path. No secrets/policy changes, no new deps, scope limited to one function. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass. Minor caveat: if a caller passes a relative projectRoot, path.resolve could yield unexpected results, but default cwd is absolute and behavior is safe.
Pure rename/refactor of fetch() params and JSDoc; argument order to #dispatch is correct and behavior-preserving. No security-sensitive paths touched. lint/type/test pass.

Only fires when _bsontype is defined and non-null (already covered by preceding == null branch), so no regression to valid BSON types. No gate relaxation. Deterministic checks pass and are consistent with the diff. Maker stdout/stderr artifacts missing but check results recorded.

Removing the array->object header conversion breaks removeMatchingHeaders for array-form headers (it iterates array indices, not names), so sensitive headers leak across host/protocol boundaries on redirect (index.js:484-490,630-640). This reverts the 'Support key/value header arrays' feature and its security guarantees; tests test.js:1759,1808 are expected to fail. The reported test:changed=pass contradicts the diff/source (stdout unavailable, maker logs missing), so evidence is inconsistent. Restore the conversion or make removeMatchingHeaders array-aware before merging.

Path-traversal fix is correct and sufficient: path.basename() closes the write-path traversal in writeExportFile, and the ValidationError in backupContent.query adds defense-in-depth at the API boundary. exportContent's read path was already sanitized via path.parse in readBackup, so no gap. Edge cases ( '..', empty string) are safe. Checks pass; no gates relaxed.

Switching from single-quoted + sanitised args to double-quoted args reintroduces command injection: double quotes still interpolate $(), backticks (mac/linux) and %VAR% (win). keys.replace('"','\\"') only escapes the first quote, and id is now unquoted on darwin. This is a security regression versus the prior sanitiser; restore single-quote quoting or use a non-shell API (execFile with arg array) / proper escaping of $ ` \ " %.

Removes the only MXID-format and cross-homeserver serverName validation from the OpenID token-exchange path, weakening an impersonation guard on a persisted/returned userId. Tests/lint/type-check pass but do not cover this invariant; advisory not independently reviewed. Security-sensitive gate relaxation, escalate.

Security regression: matchFileSnapshot drops the projectRoot parameter and the path-traversal containment check (resolved.startsWith(root + path.sep)). The function now reads/writes/mkdirs at an arbitrary caller-supplied filePath with no boundary, enabling arbitrary filesystem read/write (incl. via toMatchFileSnapshot public API at src/assertions/index.ts:1035). Existing security tests in tests/unit/snapshot-matchers.test.ts:97-114 assert that absolute and ../../../ traversal paths throw /File snapshot path must be within the project directory/; with the change those calls would instead write to /tmp and ../../../tmp/evil.snap, so assert.throws would fail. Tests at lines 38,50,62,77,90,109,121 also pass a third projectRoot argument that no longer exists in the signature (TS excess-arguments error). The reported deterministic checks (test:changed/lint/type-check all pass) contradict the diff, which only touches snapshots.ts and leaves both the failing security assertions and the now-invalid 3-arg calls in place. Preserve the containment invariant (and projectRoot param) before any such refactor; do not relax the gate.

Valid command-injection mitigation: anchored hex-only regex (7-40 chars) validates the `commit` option before it is interpolated into the git show shell command at index.ts:42. Guard correctly no-ops on empty commit and returns a typed { error } on invalid input. Deterministic checks pass. Minor stylistic nit: `new RegExp(hashRegex)` could be `hashRegex.test(...)`; no security impact.

Security-positive change: removes full refresh-token logging in src/session.ts:123/134, logging only last 10 chars of access tokens behind `debug` flag. No new sensitive exposure, no control-flow/logic changes, no gate relaxation. workos.ts is a cosmetic version bump 0.13.1->0.13.2. test:changed/lint/type-check all pass. Note: logging last 10 chars of an access token still leaks a token suffix, but this is gated behind `debug` and is materially better than the prior full-refresh-token leak.

Diff adds `!isFunction(input)` guards to evaluateWildcard (line 609) and recurseDescendants (line 680), preventing object-key traversal into jsonata functions/lambdas. Uses existing utils.isFunction helper and mirrors the established guard pattern already present in functions.js:1434/1673/1700. Minimal, consistent, defensive change. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass. No governance gates relaxed; no secrets/policy touched. Maker stdout/stderr artifacts are missing but checks pass on the diff.

Single-quote-and-strip sanitisation is a valid command-injection mitigation for the mac/linux exec sinks; no gates relaxed, no new sinks. Windows path now passes literal single quotes to the .bat (cmd.exe doesn't treat single quotes as quotes) — a functional change, not a security regression. id is now string-quoted into osascript, a possible behavior change but not a vulnerability. Deterministic checks pass.

Diff is documentation-only: corrects malformed inline YAML `env:` mapping to block style in three JSDoc comment blocks in GitHubActions.ts. No executable code, no security-relevant logic, no gates touched. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass. The changes match the stated fix and are safe.

Removes path.basename() traversal guard on caller-supplied options.fileName; path.join() resolves '..' so this reintroduces a path-traversal/arbitrary-write vector at index.js:52,64,77. Reject; restore basename (or equivalent confinement) before merging.

filteredUrl is a password-redaction function; dropping _.escapeRegExp while adding only null-safety allows regex metacharacters in passwords to cause crashes or, worse, failure to redact the credential (leak to logs). Preserve escaping: _.escapeRegExp(config.password || ''). Deterministic checks do not exercise metacharacter passwords.

Replaces shell-based exec with execFile+argv array, eliminating shell injection from path/sha. Semantics preserved (git show sha:path). test:changed, lint, type-check all pass. No gates relaxed; change is correct and safe.

Change adds case-insensitive 'bearer' scheme validation to jwk.ts:82 and jwt.ts:83, closing an auth-scheme confusion issue where non-Bearer credentials (e.g. 'Basic <b64>') would be silently parsed as a JWT/JWK token. Logic is correct, uses toLowerCase() for RFC 7235 case-insensitivity, preserves the 401 'invalid credentials structure' path and cookie fallback. No gates relaxed, no secrets/policy touched. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass on this diff.

MXID server-name validation in postExchangeOpenId is correct and security-positive: a malicious homeserver can no longer return a sub belonging to a different homeserver, preventing cross-homeserver impersonation via widget tokens. Regex/semantics align with existing server resolution (matrixServer) and IP-blacklist path; errors use ErrCode.BadOpenID consistent with surrounding code. No secrets, deps, gates, or control-flow changes. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) pass on this diff. Maker artifacts (stdout/stderr logs) missing but deterministic results are present and sufficient.

Change is correct and safe; improves redaction in the private request() debug log. Partial coverage only: stringData not redacted; SecretList/watch-event secret payloads not handled; GET (client.ts:309) and WATCH (client.ts:166) debug logs still emit raw bodies. structuredClone may throw on non-cloneable bodies but request() uses json:true so acceptable. No new vulnerability introduced; gaps are pre-existing and not a regression.

The diff removes a defense-in-depth security guard: `rejectExecutableFrontmatter` explicitly blocked .prompty frontmatter that declared a `js`/`javascript` engine, preventing gray-matter from evaluating executable frontmatter. Stripping it (`matter(raw)` with no engine overrides) re-opens the path to JS-engine frontmatter parsing, which is a security-sensitive regression with no accompanying rationale, replacement guard, or test coverage. The deterministic checks (test:changed/lint/type-check) all pass, but they are green only because nothing in the changed-test set exercises the JS-frontmatter rejection path — absence of failure is not evidence of safety. Maker artifacts (stdout/stderr logs) are also missing. Recommend restoring the `engines: { js, javascript }` overrides and the `rejectExecutableFrontmatter` function (or replacing them with an equivalent explicit rejection), and adding a regression test that asserts a .prompty file with JS frontmatter is rejected. This is a security-sensitive change and should be escalated, not merged on green checks alone.

Removes the server-signature verification (verifyTxSignedBy) from SEP-10 readChallengeTx. This breaks the documented invariant ('verified if signed by the server account') and the SEP-0010 protocol requirement; the surviving source-account check is not a signature proof and can be forged by a transaction constructor. The change is security-sensitive, contradicts the function contract, and is filed only as generic doc-drift with no exploit/failing test justifying removal. Deterministic checks pass but do not cover this invariant; maker logs are missing. Escalate as security_sensitive_change; do not relax gates.

Change reverts the #800 security fix: removing !isFunction(input) from evaluateWildcard (src/jsonata.js:609) and recurseDescendants (src/jsonata.js:680) lets * and ** enumerate internals of lambda/function objects. Verified at runtime: $sum.* returns [true,null,{definition:"<a<n>:n>"}] and $sum.** returns _jsonata_function/signature fields instead of undefined, violating test/test-suite/groups/wildcards/case010.json (undefinedResult). Security-sensitive regression; do not merge. Reported test:changed=pass contradicts the diff/source behavior and is not reliable evidence.

The diff removes a deliberately-introduced path traversal protection (commit f466c30) from both db.js (front-gate ValidationError on path separators) and export-filename.js (defense-in-depth path.basename()) with no equivalent replacement. The backupContent endpoint (permissions:true) feeds options.filename unsanitized into writeExportFile -> path.resolve(urlJoin(contentPath,'data', filename)). An authenticated admin can now supply a filename containing '../' to write the DB-export JSON to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the data/ dir (path traversal write). readBackup still sanitizes via path.parse so the export/read path is unaffected, but the backup write path is now vulnerable. Lint/type/test:changed pass because no test covered the guard — they cannot detect the security regression. This is a security-sensitive change that relaxes a gate; reject and require the sanitization (or an equivalent allowlist) to be reinstated.

session.ts:123,134 now log the full refresh token instead of a redacted suffix, a credential-exposure regression vs the prior slice(-10) redaction. workos.ts:4 also reverts the version with no rationale. Rejecting per 'do not relax gates' and security-sensitivity escalation.

The change removes an explicit security guardrail. The original code disabled HMAC-SHA1 by default and gated it behind SignedXml.enableHMAC() precisely because enabling HMAC and digital-signature (RSA) algorithms simultaneously introduces XML signature key-confusion/wrapping risk (an attacker can swap a signed RSA element for an HMAC-signed one using a shared secret). The maker enables 'hmac-sha1' unconditionally in SignatureAlgorithms alongside the RSA algos and deletes enableHMAC, doing exactly what the removed comments warned against. No compensating control (separate keyring, algorithm allowlist per key, verification-mode flag) is introduced. This relaxes a documented security gate and broadens the default attack surface for signature wrapping/confusion. Deterministic lint/type/test checks passing do not address this security regression. Recommend reverting; if HMAC support is required it should remain opt-in via an explicit enableHMAC()/allowlist mechanism that disables RSA algos or is scoped to a single key type.

Change hardens the sandbox by blocking access to `caller`, `callee`, and `arguments` on functions (prop.ts:100-102), a well-known sandbox-escape vector that leaks stack frames and external references. The guard is placed before the property read (val moved to line 104), so the dangerous access never occurs. Existing prototype/__proto__ and whitelist gates are preserved. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass on this diff. No relaxation of gates, no secret/policy changes.

Pure additive TypeScript interface (FlexVolumeSource) added to persistentvolume.ts, matching the Kubernetes core/v1 FlexVolumeSource shape (driver, fsType, secretRef, readOnly, options). Imported LocalObjectReference correctly exists at ./localobjectreference.ts. No executable code, no secrets, no policy or gate changes; only a union member added to PersistentVolumeSource. lint, type-check, and test:changed all pass. No security risk.

Additive, backward-compatible change: adds optional `address` field to deploy options, used as a preferred source for `new Address(...)` with `publicKey!` retained as fallback. No new validation is required since `Address` constructor validates input; no secrets, policy, or auth-bypass introduced. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass on this diff. Maker artifacts (stdout/stderr) are missing but the included check results suffice for this small, low-risk diff.

Small, safe change converting array-form headers ([k,v,k,v,...]) into an object inside _sanitizeOptions, gated behind Array.isArray so existing object/undefined paths are unchanged. Odd-length arrays yield undefined values but that is the caller's responsibility and not a regression. No new injection, auth, or SSRF surface; headers are already caller-controlled. No prototype pollution of shared objects (target is a fresh {}). Sensitive-headers handling preserved below. lint/type-check/test:changed all pass. Maker stdout/stderr artifacts missing but deterministic checks present and consistent with diff.

Safe, minimal change. Triple-brace raw interpolation is gated to error-message templates (T1005/T1007) and runs before the JSON.stringify double-brace pass, avoiding partial-match collisions. No injection surface (error strings only, no eval/HTML). Backward compatible with existing {{value}} templates. lint/type-check/test:changed all pass.

Change replaces raw password interpolation in `new RegExp(...)` with `_.escapeRegExp(config.password)`. lodash is imported (config-helper.js:5) so `_.escapeRegExp` is available. This fixes a regex-injection / broken-redaction bug where password metacharacters (`.`, `*`, `+`, `(`, etc.) would alter matching; `_.escapeRegExp(undefined)` returns '' so the previous `|| ''` fallback behavior is preserved. Pure defensive hardening of a credential-redaction helper, no new attack surface, no gates relaxed. lint/type-check/test:changed all pass. Artifacts stdout/stderr missing but deterministic results are present and consistent with the diff.

The diff reverts the NODE-2514 security fix (commit 3809c13) by deleting the TypeError guard on unrecognized _bsontype in all three serializeInto branches. This reintroduces silent value-dropping during serialization (data integrity regression) and is inconsistent with the untouched calculate_size.js path. Deterministic checks pass but do not cover this guard; no maker rationale/artifacts provided. Do not merge.

The change reverts a deliberate security mitigation: it replaces execFile (no-shell, argv array) with exec (shell) and interpolates unsanitized sha and path directly into the command string. path is only wrapped in double quotes, which is trivially bypassable via embedded quotes/metacharacters (e.g. path containing \"; cmd; \"), enabling command injection. sha is also unvalidated. The removed comment explicitly documented this protection. Deterministic checks (lint/type/test) passing does not cover injection risk. Reject; restore execFile with argv array and add input validation if needed.

The diff removes src/security.ts and the redactResponseBodyForLogging call in src/client.ts:93, causing Kubernetes Secret objects (body.kind === 'Secret') to be logged verbatim via debug() including the base64-encoded `data` field. This is a secret-disclosure regression, not a doc-drift/small fix: the redaction control is deleted rather than preserved. While lint/type-check/test:changed pass, that does not validate the removed security invariant. Original failure: none described; this change weakens an existing security gate and must be reverted or the redaction reimplemented (and ideally unit-tested) before acceptance.

Replaces execFileSync (no shell, arg-array) with execSync (shell-interpolated) across gitMergeBase, gitFetch, listShas, and listParentCommits, interpolating external base/head/ref/target/sha/path values directly into shell command strings. This is a command-injection regression and a relaxation of the prior safe-exec invariant; no input validation or shell-quoting was added. Revert to execFileSync with argument arrays (or add proper shell escaping) before merge. Deterministic checks pass but do not cover injection vectors; maker stdout/stderr artifacts are missing.

Security hardening: HMAC-SHA1 disabled by default to prevent key-confusion; opt-in via SignedXml.enableHMAC() which restricts the map to HMAC-only. Default rsa-sha1 path preserved. findSignatureAlgorithm throws on unsupported algos (no silent fallback). No gates relaxed. Deterministic checks pass. Minor gap: maker stdout/stderr artifacts missing, but included check results suffice.

Removes the caller/callee/arguments access guard on functions (prop.ts) with no replacement. These are well-known sandbox-escape primitives (stack-frame leakage); deleting the check relaxes a security gate. Passing lint/type/changed tests do not cover this vector, so safety is not demonstrated. Recommend restoring the guard (or moving it, not deleting it).

Change converts execSync (shell) calls to execFileSync (no shell) in packages/core/src/ci-environment/git.ts, eliminating shell-injection risk in gitMergeBase, gitFetch, listShas, and listParentCommits. Behavior preserved (same args/flags); String(input.depth) correctly coerces numeric depth. No new error handling, secrets, or policy changes introduced. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass. Maker artifacts (stdout/stderr logs) are missing but checks pass on the diff and source. Safe, security-positive change.

Security hardening: path.basename on caller-supplied fileName prevents path traversal when joined into tempDir at index.js:52,64. path already imported; behavior preserved for valid basenames; downstream ext/slice logic intact. All deterministic checks pass. No governance relaxation.

db:seed:undo:all now reads executed seeders (via migrator.executed()) instead of pending ones before calling migrator.down(), which is the correct set to unseed. Deterministic checks (test:changed, lint, type-check) all pass.

Rejects JS/javascript frontmatter engines in gray-matter by replacing their parse fn with one that throws, preventing code execution from .prompty frontmatter while leaving default YAML parsing intact. Change is small, scoped, and correct; checks pass.

Removing the Bearer scheme check from jwk.ts/jwt.ts weakens the RFC 6750 Authorization contract (any scheme prefix now accepted while WWW-Authenticate still advertises Bearer) and breaks unmodified existing tests that assert non-Bearer schemes are rejected (jwt/index.test.ts:87, jwk/index.test.ts:83,421,551). test:changed passing is not credible evidence: no test:changed script exists in package.json and the test files were not in the diff, so the scheme-rejection tests were likely not executed; stdout/stderr artifacts are also missing. Core JWT signature verification is preserved, so not an auth bypass, but the change regresses a security-relevant invariant and should be revised or accompanied by updated tests/contract.

Server-signature check added to readChallengeTx via existing verifyTxSignedBy helper; enforced across all SEP-10 verification paths and tightens (not relaxes) the security gate. Deterministic checks pass.

Safe relaxation: removes an over-broad lone-backslash ban while keeping `..`-segment and double-separator traversal protections intact. path.join keeps paths within root; encoded backslashes are decoded pre-check so no bypass. Deterministic checks pass and the mixed-separator traversal test at test/serve-static.test.ts:361 remains satisfied.

Removing hashRegex validation reintroduces command injection via the unsanitized 'commit' option passed to execa.commandSync (shell-parsed) at index.ts:37. The hex regex was the sole input guard. Restore validation or switch to execa's execa(...args) form with argument array (no shell parsing) before this can be accepted.

The diff adds `|\\` to the path-traversal guard regex in src/serve-static.ts:81, rejecting any filename containing a backslash. This is a strict tightening (blocks more inputs, never fewer), preventing backslash-based path traversal on platforms/paths where backslashes act as separators. No regressions in traversal protection; lint, type-check, and changed tests all pass. No secrets, policy, or governance invariants affected.
